instructions: Peel the potatoes and cut them into 1-inch chunks. Transfer them to a pot, cover with cold water and add 1/2 tsp salt. Bring to a boil over high heat, then simmer for 12 to 15 minutes, until a fork slides in easily. Drain well.
While the potatoes cook, remove the stems and seeds from 2 of the dried chilies. Transfer them to a small bowl and cover with hot water. Leave them for 20 minutes.

Make the dabeli masala. Set a small dry skillet over medium-low heat and add the remaining dried chili, the coriander seeds, cinnamon, cloves and 1/2 tsp of the cumin seeds. Stir for about 1 minute, until fragrant.
Transfer the spices to a plate and let them cool for 3 minutes. Grind them to a fine powder in a spice grinder or blender. That should be about 2 tsp.

Drain the soaked chilies and transfer them to a blender with the garlic, the lemon juice and a pinch of salt. Blend to a smooth paste, adding a splash of water if needed. This is the red garlic chutney.
Mash the drained potatoes in a bowl until mostly smooth. Finely chop the onion and set aside 1/3 cup for the filling.
Set a large skillet over medium heat and add the oil and the remaining 1/2 tsp cumin seeds. After about 20 seconds the seeds will crackle.
Add the 1/3 cup onion and cook for 3 minutes, until soft. Add the asafoetida and stir for 10 seconds.

Stir in 2 tbsp of the tamarind chutney, then add the mashed potatoes, 1 1/2 tsp of the dabeli masala and 1/2 tsp salt. Cook for 3 minutes, stirring often, and add a splash of water if it looks dry. Take the pan off the heat and stir in 2 tbsp chopped cilantro.
Split the pav rolls through the side, leaving one edge attached. Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat and toast the rolls for about 1 minute per side, until lightly golden.
Spread about 1 tsp tamarind chutney on the top half of each roll and about 1 tsp of the red garlic chutney on the bottom half.

Fill each roll with about 1/4 cup of the potato filling. Top with the remaining chopped onion, 1/4 cup chopped cilantro, the peanuts, the pomegranate seeds, a pinch of the leftover dabeli masala and the sev. Close the rolls and serve warm.

To pack it for lunch, keep the filling in a container and the rolls and toppings separate. The filling keeps for 3 days in the fridge. Reheat it in a skillet over medium heat with a splash of water, then fill the rolls.
method_notes: Veg Recipes of India (the lead, 4.86 from 27 ratings) builds Kutchi dabeli from a spiced potato filling cooked with a homemade dabeli masala (red chili, coriander, cinnamon, cloves, cumin) and sweet tamarind chutney, served in toasted pav with a red garlic chutney, peanuts, pomegranate and sev. Only this source was read in full. This follows the lead, scaled to 8 rolls, without the optional coconut. It takes about 55 minutes, so it works as a make-ahead lunch, not a 30 minute one.
